lines: # Adaptive rejection sampling for a univariate log-concave density.
# Base R only. Sourcing this file has no side effects; run test() explicitly.
.ars_stop(name, " must be an integer between ", minimum,
# Wrap a vectorized function, expression(), or quote() in a checked log-density.
.ars_stop("density must be a vectorized function or an expression in x.")
eval(density, envir = c(list(x = x), args), enclos = envir)
.ars_stop("Density must return one finite numeric value per x (vectorized). ",
"Use log = TRUE for densities that underflow.")
.ars_stop("Density must be strictly positive inside domain; check domain ",
"or use log = TRUE to avoid underflow.")
# Numerical log derivative: Richardson-extrapolated central differences. Never
# evaluate at/outside the declared boundaries. Analytic derivatives are preferred
# for extremely narrow, steep, or nonsmooth targets.
if (!is.function(derivative)) .ars_stop("derivative must be a function or NULL.")
.ars_stop("derivative must return one finite log-density derivative per x.")
if (any(!is.finite(step) | step <= 0 | x + step == x | x - step == x))
.ars_stop("Cannot calculate numerical log derivatives; supply derivative.")
# For a concave h, h'(x_i) >= chord slope >= h'(x_{i+1}). This
# simultaneously checks decreasing derivatives and consistency with h itself.
slack <- tolerance * pmax(1, abs(secant), abs(head(d, -1L)), abs(tail(d, -1L)))
"(or the supplied log derivative is incorrect).")
# Integral of exp(h + d*(t-x)) on [a,b], calculated entirely in log space.
.ars_stop("Non-integrable envelope: a flat tail needs a finite boundary.")
if (!is.finite(b)) .ars_stop("Non-integrable envelope: right tail slope must be negative.")
return(h + d * (b - x) + base::log(-expm1(-d * (b - a))) - base::log(d))
if (!is.finite(a)) .ars_stop("Non-integrable envelope: left tail slope must be positive.")
h + d * (a - x) + base::log(-expm1(d * (b - a))) - base::log(-d)
.ars_stop("Non-integrable envelope: initial points must have a positive left ",
"tail slope and a negative right tail slope on unbounded sides.")
z[j] <- x[j] + (h[j + 1L] - h[j] - d[j + 1L] * dx[j]) / delta[j]
z <- c(domain[1L], pmax(head(x, -1L), pmin(tail(x, -1L), z)), domain[2L])
.ars_stop("Numerically invalid envelope masses; rescale the target or domain.")
list(x = x, h = h, d = d, z = z, log_mass = mass, weight = weight / sum(weight))
# Inverse CDF of a single exponential piece, including flat and infinite pieces.
if (d > 0) return(b + log1p((1 - u) * expm1(-d * (b - a))) / d)
if (!is.finite(x)) .ars_stop("Non-finite envelope proposal; rescale the domain.")
list(x = x, upper = hull$h[j] + hull$d[j] * (x - hull$x[j]))
.ars_stop("initial must contain at least two distinct finite points strictly inside domain.")
# Geometric tail search is only automatic when the user omitted initial.
if (attempt == 50L) .ars_stop("Cannot bracket integrable tails; supply initial/domain.")
# Audit midpoints as well, before any squeeze can accept a proposal.
#' Sample from a positive, integrable, log-concave density on one interval.
#' n: nonnegative integer sample count; density: vectorized function or quoted
#' expression in x. ... supplies named arguments to density (or expression).
#' domain: increasing c(lower, upper), possibly infinite, containing exactly the
#' target support; finite endpoints need not have positive density.
#' initial: >=2 distinct interior points; for infinite sides their log slopes must
#' point inward. NULL chooses points and attempts geometric tail bracketing.
#' log: TRUE if density returns log density. derivative: optional vectorized
#' derivative OF THE LOG DENSITY, with target parameters captured in its closure.
#' tolerance: relative tolerance for numerical concavity checks.
#' max_points: cap on stored support points (checks continue after the cap).
#' max_iter: hard proposal limit; failure returns an error, never partial samples.
#' squeeze: use chord squeezing to avoid some density evaluations. FALSE evaluates
#' and checks the density at EVERY proposal, useful for additional auditing.
#' Returns a plain numeric vector, using R's normal RNG / set.seed(). Numerical
#' derivatives approximate tangents; provide an analytic derivative for demanding
#' precision. Finite checks cannot prove global concavity of an arbitrary function:
#' the caller must supply a log-concave target; violations found are fatal.
#'   ars(1000, dexp, domain = c(0, Inf), rate = 2)
#'   ars(1000, function(x) dnorm(x, log = TRUE), log = TRUE,
ars <- function(n, density, initial = NULL, domain = c(-Inf, Inf),
.ars_stop("domain must be two increasing numeric bounds, e.g. c(0, Inf).")
.ars_stop("tolerance must be positive and at most 0.001.")
.ars_stop("Extra density arguments must have unique names other than x.")
.ars_stop("max_points must accommodate initial points and their midpoint audit (",
.ars_stop("max_iter exceeded after accepting ", accepted, " of ", n, " samples.")
if (hx > upper + slack || (is.finite(lower) && hx < lower - slack))
.ars_stop("Non-log-concave density detected during sampling: target violates hull bounds ",
# Check a new point even when the storage cap prevents adaptation.
# Use the PRE-UPDATE envelope and the SAME uniform for rejection.
# Formal tests: deterministic unit/error checks plus seeded distribution checks.
# Each case prints NAME: PASS/FAIL and mean/sd (NA for non-sampling cases).
# Distribution acceptance uses a six-standard-error mean bound, variance bounds
# using the known fourth central moment, and a DKW bound on empirical-CDF error.
# At alpha=1e-6 per CDF comparison, random false failures are deliberately rare.
# RNG state/kind are restored on exit. Return a data frame with details invisibly;
# any failure is fatal by default so CI/Rscript receives a nonzero exit status.
test <- function(n = 10000L, seed = 1992L, output_dir = "/app", stop_on_failure = TRUE) {
mean = unname(stats[1L]), sd = unname(stats[2L]), detail = detail)
close <- function(a, b, tol = 1e-7) all(abs(a - b) <= tol * pmax(1, abs(b)))
distribution <- function(samples, mu, variance, fourth, cdf, support = c(-Inf, Inf)) {
d <- max(seq_len(m) / m - u, u - (seq_len(m) - 1) / m)
pass = all(is.finite(samples)) && all(samples >= support[1L] & samples <= support[2L]) &&
detail = sprintf("truth mean=%.6f sd=%.6f; CDF D=%.5f <= %.5f",
truth <- integrate(function(x) exp(v[3L] * x), v[1L], v[2L])$value
recovered <- vapply(q, function(v) exp(.ars_log_mass(-2, v, 0, 0, d)) / total, numeric(1))
record("INVALID_COUNTS", all(vapply(list(-1, 1.5, NA_real_, Inf, c(1, 2), "3", TRUE),
record("INVALID_DOMAINS", all(vapply(list(c(1, 0), c(0, 0), c(NA, 1), 1, c(Inf, Inf)),
function(v) expect_error(ars(1, dnorm, domain = v), "domain"), logical(1))))
record("INVALID_INITIAL_POINTS", all(vapply(list(c(1, 1), c(NA, 1), 0, c(0, Inf), c(-1, 2)),
function(v) expect_error(ars(1, dexp, domain = c(0, Inf), initial = v), "initial"), logical(1))))
expect_error(ars(1, dnorm, derivative = function(x) NA_real_), "derivative must") &&
expect_error(ars(1, function(x) rep(1, length(x)), initial = c(-1, 1)), "Non-integrable") &&
expect_error(ars(1, function(x) exp(x), initial = c(0.2, 1), domain = c(0, Inf)), "Non-integrable")
# Identical to N(0,1) near the initial hull but log-convex in the tails.
# No initial audit sees the violation; proposals outside it must detect it.
expect_error(ars(1000, bad, log = TRUE, initial = c(-0.1, 0, 0.1),
row.names = FALSE, col.names = FALSE, quote = FALSE)
exponential <- ars(n, dexp, domain = c(0, Inf), rate = 2)
row.names = FALSE, col.names = FALSE, quote = FALSE)
ars(n, dgamma, domain = c(0, Inf), shape = 3, rate = 2),
ars(n, dbeta, domain = c(0, 1), shape1 = 2, shape2 = 3),
ars(n, dunif, domain = c(-2, 4), min = -2, max = 4),
ars(n, function(x) 1000 - (x-10)^2/8, log = TRUE, initial = c(6, 10, 14),
distribution(ars(n, dnorm, domain = c(a, b)), mu, m2-mu^2, central4,
cat(sprintf("\n%d/%d tests passed. Sample files: %s\n", sum(result$passed),
if (stop_on_failure && any(!result$passed)) .ars_stop("Formal tests failed; see FAIL lines above.")
